6856667354597115191: The tradition of eating pastries during the Double Ninth Festival dates back to the Han Dynasty. The "Miscellaneous Records of the Western Capital" notes, "On the ninth day of the ninth month, wear dogwood, eat peng cakes, drink Chrysanthemum Wine, and live a long life." Here, "peng cakes" refer to pastries. By the Song Dynasty, the custom of eating pastries during the festival became widespread. The "Jade Candle Treasury" records, "On the ninth day, eating cakes and drinking Chrysanthemum Wine coincides with the harvest of millet and sorghum, celebrating the season's bounty and forming a lasting tradition." The Five-Colored Cake is one such festive pastry, where "eating cake" symbolizes "ascending heights," and "five colors" represent the "five grains," embodying wishes for prosperity and a plentiful harvest.
